form:HelpHTML.p: The temporal store supplying the map's time-varying events — for example people or vehicles whose position changes over time. Events are drawn as the overlay that moves (and leaves a fading trail) as the timeline plays.

Must be a FloorMap Event Store, which is the document type that fixes the key encoding the map's point-in-time read needs, and that carries the event expiry. Leave blank if the map has no moving events.
The temporal store supplying the map's facts — the longer-lived content such as background images, gates, desks and rooms.

Each fact is versioned over time, so the map shows how the space was arranged at the moment selected on the timeline. This is also the store the Editor tab reads and writes, and the one Discover (below) scans for types.
Must be an SQL Temporal Store.
How each stored entry's value is encoded. The Value Schema paths below are interpreted against this format.

ul.li: JSON — paths are JSON field names, e.g. .type or .coords.
XML — paths address elements/attributes within the XML value.

form:HelpHTML.p: Set this to match how your feed or pipeline writes the store. Changing it re-interprets every entry, so only change it if the stored format really changed.

Tells the map how to read each stored value by mapping a Role (what the renderer needs) to a Path within the value. Display Name is an optional label for the field and Default is used when the field is absent from an entry.

ul.li: Type — the fact's type; drives paint order and the default graphic (configured on the Layers panel).
Label — the name shown on the map.
Position — the world coordinates [x, y] of a point fact.
Image — an Asset Store image URL. A fact with an image is drawn as a scaled image; a background is simply an image fact.
World-to-Map — a 6-element affine matrix [a, b, c, d, e, f] that positions, scales and rotates the fact in map space.

form:HelpHTML.p: Use the toolbar to add or remove a mapping.
Counts the events behind the timeline's density bars. Returns one row per bucket, which is what keeps its size bounded by the visible range rather than by how many events the store holds.
The bucket width arrives as param('bucketWidth') and changes as you zoom, so leave that alone. Add a where clause to count only some events.
Finds the first and last event times, which is what the timeline's Show All button fits to.

Deliberately unbounded: a time bound here could never reach data earlier than what is already shown, which is the one thing Show All exists to do. Note that a where clause narrows the extent, so Show All would fit to the filtered subset rather than to the store.
